text: Getting started Your agent, in two lines. A program of your own names what its agent loads, then starts a host. This is the coding agent's whole Program.cs, as it runs in the terminal. The call at the bottom is all the code it takes. The host lends the rest, which is web access, telemetry and the model providers. You write the program, its catalogue, your identities and your settings. The engine, the hosts and the packs are the framework's. Today your project references them from this repo, and packaging them for NuGet is planned. Program.cs CodingCatalog Yours. The program starts a host, and the catalogue names the identities and packs it loads. identity/ config/ Yours too. Who your agent is, as markdown you can read, and the settings it runs with. LouisAgent.Core LouisAgent.Cli The framework's. The engine runs the loop, and this host puts it in the terminal. packs/tools/ Ready-made packs. Each one is something an agent can do, and you name it in your catalogue or leave it out. Engine, identities and packs The folders say what ships Where it stands Its settings, then run it. Each program reads the settings in its own config folder, and the first place that sets a name wins. With the .NET 10 SDK installed, three steps get the coding agent answering. your shell What is set already wins, so one run can switch, as LLM_PROFILE=ollama dotnet run does. .env.secrets Your keys, kept out of git. .env The demo's settings. .env.{LLM_PROFILE} The model's own, such as .env.ollama or .env.anthropic , read last. Copy the settings. Copy demos/louis-agent/config/.env.example to .env beside it, and .env.secrets.example to .env.secrets . Name a model. Put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env.secrets , or pick a local model through Ollama with LLM_PROFILE=ollama . Run it. From demos/louis-agent/hosts/LouisAgent.CodingCli , type dotnet run . Its launch profile points it at the demo's config/ folder. How settings are loaded Every setting Where next Then make it yours. Once it answers, change who it is, give it tools of your own, or put it on a website with a chat. Each guide walks one of those through, start to finish.
